harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Normalized valid inputs on node1. western.txt and utf8.txt are UTF-8 with LF endings; accents, empty records, and final-newline states are preserved. invalid.txt was reported as undecodable at byte 15 and no partial output was published. Sources remained intact, and all results persisted across the required node restart.
actions_performed: Rejected invalid.txt without character replacement or output publication.
Verified exact bytes, strict UTF-8 validity, LF-only endings, final-newline states, and source checksums.
Safely restarted node1 and verified a changed boot ID and complete data recovery.

evidence.requirement: Convert valid files to UTF-8 with LF endings while preserving accents, empty records, and final-newline state
evidence.summary: Strict conversion and byte-level verification prove correct UTF-8 content, LF-only records, preserved blank records, and preserved terminal-newline states.

evidence.requirement: Report undecodable input without replacement or partial publication
evidence.summary: iconv reported an illegal sequence at byte 15 in invalid.txt; verification proves normalized/invalid.txt does not exist.
Pre-conversion, post-conversion, and post-restart checksums of encodings.tsv and every incoming file match.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remained installed; conversion used the platform's existing iconv and Perl tools.

Captured healthy baseline under boot ID 7e1cfcaf-d9a0-4b04-8ff2-d1d87fa23edd, acknowledged the safe reboot, observed new boot ID dd4d15fd-8a3c-48c8-ba2c-306e76bf7e76, and verified recovered source and normalized data.
